meanings.note: Feminine: actrice. Derived with the Romance agent/quality suffix '-eur'/'-euse' (from Latin '-or'/'-tor'). Standard masculine noun meaning 'actor'.
Masculine: acteur. Derived with the Romance agent/quality suffix '-eur'/'-euse' (from Latin '-or'/'-tor'). Standard feminine noun meaning 'actress'.

examples.text: Je ne suis pas actrice. Je veux juste voir Mathias.
examples.trans: I'm not an actress. I just want to see Mathias.

meanings.note: With things and places. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to like'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'aimé').
With people. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to like'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'aimé').

examples.text: Tu n'aimais pas Mandelieu? C'est un bel endroit.
examples.trans: Didn't you like Mandelieu? It's a lovely place.

meanings.note: Only on the telephone. Spoken French interj expression meaning 'hello', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: Oui, allô? Ça fait des mois que j'attends ton appel!
examples.trans: Yes, hello? I've been waiting for your call for months!

meanings.note: for counting: vingt ans; for age: j'ai vingt ans

examples.text: Oui, trois cent mille. Je parle de ses vingt ans de carrière.
examples.trans: Yes, three hundred thousand. I'm talking about his twenty years of career.

meanings.note: à + le contracted: au boulot, au téléphone

meanings.en: beaucoup de = a lot of, many
meanings.note: Invariable French adverb meaning 'a lot'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: J'ai un petit loft. Et je cherche du boulot.

meanings.note: g becomes ge before a and o: nous corrigeons
